Integer division (x DIV y in Hive, Spark and MySQL, x // y in DuckDB, DIV(x, y) in BigQuery) truncates towards zero, but sqlglot's rewrite for dialects without an integer-division operator does not preserve that: Presto gets CAST(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y AS INTEGER), which rounds instead of truncating and can overflow, and the generic integer-division cast (also produced by the Python expression builder, x // 1) uses INT instead of BIGINT. Separately, a one-argument TRUNC(n) from Oracle or Snowflake transpiled to MySQL must give a valid TRUNCATE call with an explicit 0 decimals argument.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT x DIV y", read="hive", write="presto")[0]
# currently: SELECT CAST(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y AS INTEGER)
# expected:  SELECT CAST(TRUNCATE(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y) AS BIGINT)

(exp.column("x") // 1).sql()
# currently: CAST(x / 1 AS INT)
# expected:  CAST(x / 1 AS BIGINT)

transpile("SELECT TRUNC(3.14159)", read="oracle", write="mysql")[0]
# currently: SELECT TRUNCATE(3.14159)
# expected:  SELECT TRUNCATE(3.14159, 0)
```

Integer division (x DIV y in Hive, Spark and MySQL, x // y in DuckDB, DIV(x, y) in BigQuery) truncates towards zero, but sqlglot's rewrite for dialects without an integer-division operator does not preserve that: Presto gets CAST(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y AS INTEGER), which rounds instead of truncating and can overflow, and the generic integer-division cast (also produced by the Python expression builder, x // 1) uses INT instead of BIGINT. Separately, a one-argument TRUNC(n) from Oracle or Snowflake transpiled to MySQL must give a valid TRUNCATE call with an explicit 0 decimals argument.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT x DIV y", read="hive", write="presto")[0]
# currently: SELECT CAST(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y AS INTEGER)
# expected:  SELECT CAST(TRUNCATE(CAST(x AS DOUBLE) / y) AS BIGINT)

(exp.column("x") // 1).sql()
# currently: CAST(x / 1 AS INT)
# expected:  CAST(x / 1 AS BIGINT)

transpile("SELECT TRUNC(3.14159)", read="oracle", write="mysql")[0]
# currently: SELECT TRUNCATE(3.14159)
# expected:  SELECT TRUNCATE(3.14159, 0)
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
